blocks.raw:
<Tabs defaultTab="type-I">
  <Tab label="Type I (3-4 hr)" value="type-I">
    **Most fire-resistive** — Reinforced concrete or protected steel. Columns/beams: 3-4 hours. Floors: 2-3 hours. Used for high-rises and hazardous occupancies.
  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Type II (2 hr)" value="type-II">
    **Moderate fire resistance** — Protected steel or heavy timber. Columns: 2 hours. Used for mid-rise commercial and institutional.
  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Type III (1 hr)" value="type-III">
    **Basic protection** — Masonry bearing walls with protected steel or wood. 1-hour rating throughout. Common for low-rise commercial.
  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Type IV (Heavy Timber)" value="type-IV">
    **Massive wood members** — Columns min 8" thick, floors min 4". No concealed spaces. Mills, warehouses, churches.
  </Tab>
  <Tab label="Type V (Unprotected)" value="type-V">
    **No fire rating required** — Wood frame, light-gauge steel. Single-family, small multi-family under 3 stories.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

blocks.raw:
<LawCallout code="pd1096" section="Rule IV - Fire-Resistive Construction">


Per PD 1096, Rule VI, Sec. 603, a reinforced concrete column with all faces exposed requires a minimum dimension of 450 mm for four-hour fire resistance. A Highly Fire Restrictive Zone requires construction assemblies of not less than three to four-hour fire-resistive construction (per Rule V, Sec. 507-c), so the four-hour standard applies. A 300 mm column satisfies the two-hour requirement only. Option A is incorrect — 300 mm is the 2-hour standard; the 1-hour standard is 200 mm. Option C incorrectly applies the Fire Restrictive Zone exterior wall standard to the column dimension requirement. Option D fabricates a restriction that does not exist in the Code — RC columns are the standard structural element for Type V buildings.


</LawCallout>
